beatpool

Moment pooling of PCA bases for ECG heartbeats

beatpool represents heartbeats with patient-specific principal component bases, pools those bases across sites without sharing raw signals, and provides the reconstruction, clustering and stability tools used in the accompanying study. A pure-R reader for WFDB headers, signals and annotations is included, so the full pipeline runs without external WFDB software.

Why pool bases?

Each recording has its own covariance structure, so a basis fitted on one patient is not directly comparable with a basis fitted on another. Pooling the bases entry by entry fails because principal components are defined up to signs, permutations and rotations. beatpool offers two families of solutions:

  • Alignment-based pooling removes the indeterminacy with an orthogonal Procrustes rotation and then averages, or takes the orthogonal Procrustes mean (the default), the column-normalised mean or a QR retraction.
  • Moment pooling never aligns anything. Each site sends its leading eigenpairs \((Q_h, \lambda_h)\) and the server assembles \(\hat\Sigma = \sum_h w_h Q_h \Lambda_h Q_h'\). The outer product is invariant to any orthogonal transformation of \(Q_h\), and the leading eigenvectors of \(\hat\Sigma\) are Eckart-Young optimal for the pooled second moment.

Installation 

# from a local clone
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_local("beatpool", dependencies = TRUE)

Quick start 

library(beatpool)

sim <- simulate_beats(H = 8, n = 200, p = 61, q = 10,
                      model = "heterogeneous", epsilon = 0.2, seed = 1)
bases <- extract_bases(sim$X, q = 10)

pooled <- pool_bases(bases, method = "procrustes")   # aligned mean
spec   <- pool_spectral(bases, q = 10)               # moment pooling

reconstruction_error(sim$X[[1]], pooled$T, k = 10)
reconstruction_error(sim$X[[1]], spec$T, k = 10)

# every operator in the paper, with its communication cost
all <- pool_all(sim$X, q = 10)
attr(all, "numbers")

Reading a MIT-BIH record requires only the .hea, .dat and .atr files:

x <- read_wfdb("100", dir = "data/mitdb")
ann <- read_annotations("data/mitdb/atr/100.atr")
X <- prepare_record(x$MLII, ann, record = "100", fs = 360, wsize = 30)
b <- pca_basis(X, q = 10)
